title: EU wants ‘closest possible relationship’ with UK after agreeing Brexit reset deal – live
summary:
President of European Council says EU ‘remains open to have the closest possible relationship’ with the UK

Senior correspondent

Making today’s reset deal contingent on a further agreement on the level of tuition fees for EU citizens is designed to neutralise the leverage London gets in the next six months, EU sources have said.

Senior diplomats had already confirmed this week that the EU would defer the deal on the level of tuition fees for another six months, a move designed to give the UK leverage in parallel negotiations to have the UK included in Made in Europe legislation designed to protect EU supply chains against China.

But the move to make the food and drink deal also contingent on a tuition fees deal effectively seeks to neutralise the leverage the UK gets today.

This is a serious chess game and shows the EU, again, is willing to speak very warmly about the UK but will play absolute hard ball when it comes to conceding any points to a former member state.

It was the same point France was making last night insisting the UK could not have voting rights on legislation in relation to food and drink.

During his meeting with businesses in Brussels, PM Burnham said his EU deal would add up to 0.5% to the UK’s GDP.

“We’re pretty much there, and it’s a really good deal.”

“Treasury analysis out today is saying that now it’s clear up to 0.5% on GDP as a result of the deal. The single biggest growth intervention in this Parliament.”

title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

The international court of justice (ICJ) verdict making Myanmar the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide does not just deliver justice for Rohingya victims. It also gives the 1948 genocide convention new relevance in governing the actions of nation states.

In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.

Continue reading...

title: China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars
summary:
Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’

China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.

The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

Continue reading...

title: Trump accused of falling asleep during Xi Jinping speech at Apec summit in China
summary:
US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake

Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China.

The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.

title: ‘Everyone struggled for this justice’: tears in court as Rohingya vindicated in Myanmar genocide ruling
summary:
Relief in the immediate aftermath of a landmark ruling, but what happens next is in the hands of governments around the world

There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh as the scattered communities of Rohingya watched the UN’s top court rule the Myanmar military had committed genocide against them.

For almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape. More than 10,000 Rohingya were killed and 700,000 fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.

title: New page in history? Xi, Trump and Putin summit was more of a footnote
summary:
Far from the grand ambitions declared in Yalta in 1945, Shenzhen felt like a meeting in search of an agenda

It is arguably true, given it was the first such meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US, that Thursday’s gathering in Shenzhen deserved the description of “historic”.

But in terms of tangible outcomes, it is unlikely to warrant the “new page in the history of diplomacy” that Vladimir Putin claimed had been written, and will instead be consigned to a smallish footnote in any future volume of the 21st century.

title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules
summary:
Judgment finds ‘intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population’ after case seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of state crimes

Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military campaign, the world’s highest court has ruled, in a historic and unprecedented decision.

The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.

title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza
summary:
First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu

The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.

Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

title: Eight injured after driver in Israel repeatedly rams car into Palestinians
summary:
Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage shows driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim

Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel.

Footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported.

title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
summary: From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions. But these signals are increasingly being blocked or faked – and civilians are paying the price.

title: Peacekeeping: With 500 paternity and child support claims unresolved, UN scales up accountability
summary: The UN is adding new accountability measures to better support children fathered by peacekeepers, the Under-Secretary-General for Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance, Catherine Pollard, announced Thursday.

title: ‘Losing the battle’: AI hands predators new ways to target children
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is handing predators and criminal groups new ways to groom, extort and exploit children, while efforts to protect them are failing to keep pace, senior UN officials warned on Thursday.

title: COP31: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
summary: A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday. While activists delivered the message with humour, it reflected a serious concern: explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels had disappeared from the latest draft climate agreement. On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still trying to bridge sharp differences as civil society groups pressed for stronger action.

title: No government approval needed to form or join a group, UN rights committee says
summary: People do not need their government’s permission to form or join an association, the UN Human Rights Committee said on Thursday, issuing new guidance as civic space shrinks around the world.

title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
summary: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar on the application of the Genocide Convention, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State.

title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
summary:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

title: The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
summary: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during military operations in the northern Rakhine state in 2017.

title: Anthropic raises more than $100B in IPO. And, Dems nominate Jeffries for House speaker
summary: Despite growing concern over a possible AI bubble, Anthropic had a record-breaking initial public offering. And, Hakeem Jeffries could become the first Black Speaker of the House.

title: Violent protests and killings in Bangladesh ahead of exiled Sheikh Hasina’s planned return
summary:
Awami League party called for ⁠nationwide protest on Thursday after the government rejected Hasina’s request for passport

Parts of Bangladesh were shut down Thursday as protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina sparked clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks, with the ancestral home ⁠of former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in the violence.

Hasina’s Awami League party had called for a ​week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support ‌for Hasina’s planned return in December, culminating in a ‌nationwide lockdown on Thursday.

title: Top House Democrat questions what Trump accomplished in Xi-Putin summit
summary: Rep. Gregory Meeks raises concerns about U.S. alliances after Trump's summit with Xi and Putin. He also discusses Chinese espionage amid the Nvidia scandal.

title: Iran's attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz escalate
summary: Iran takes the offensive with attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and airstrikes on several countries around the Persian Gulf.

title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance
summary: President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin have gathered in Shenzhen, China, for a historic trilateral meeting, with Ukraine, Iran and nuclear disarmament on the agenda.

title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
summary:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Continue reading...

title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
summary:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse

A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

Continue reading...

title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military
summary:
Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago

Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions
summary:
Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu

Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.

Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed.

title: Karl Kani dressed hip-hop royalty for decades. Now he's telling his own story
summary: On NPR's Morning Edition, fashion designer Karl Kani talks about his new memoir, dressing some of hip-hop's biggest stars and why skinny jeans aren't for everyone.

title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
summary: With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can be called “just” if poorer countries cannot afford it.

title: Patients running out of options as antibiotics stop working against common infections
summary: Common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to front-line and even “last-resort” antibiotics, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Wednesday, warning that the situation today is worse than it was in 2019.

title: Dozens more children killed in Yemen amid escalating hostilities
summary: The UN child rights agency, UNICEF, on Wednesday called for warring parties in Yemen to protect children as renewed conflict between Houthi rebels and Government forces approaches the three-month mark.

title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
summary:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Continue reading...

title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
summary:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans

The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

Continue reading...

title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
summary:
St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

Continue reading...

title: Ukraine: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
summary: This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

title: World News in Brief: Ebola cases double in DR Congo, chemical exposure starts before birth, Türk concern over EU-Rwanda transfer plan
summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has more than doubled in three months, with more than 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths now reported in 67 health zones across eight provinces, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.

title: COP31: The push to protect warming oceans reaches the negotiating table
summary: From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday. Yet turning innovation into action remains a challenge, with funding gaps persisting and ministers struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance as negotiations enter their final days.

title: Haiti: ‘Atrocious abuses’ continue as UN warns anti-gang operations must priortise civilian protection
summary: The UN human rights office, OHCHR has urged greater protection for civilians in Haiti amid ongoing “atrocious abuses” committed by gangs and intensified security operations.

summary: The World Food Programme (WFP) is assisting thousands of families who fled recent violence in Ethiopia for the Moyale area in neighbouring Kenya, the UN agency reported on Tuesday.

title: Winter rains deepen Gaza crisis amid restricted access and aid cuts
summary: Gaza is facing a deepening shelter, sanitation and food security crisis as winter rains flood makeshift shelters, destroy scarce food supplies and leave displaced families struggling to stay warm and fed.

summary: Children from across the world sent a message of peace from the Omani capital Muscat on Monday, calling for an end to hatred, respect for diversity and the protection of human rights.

title: ‘An unfulfilled plan helps no one’: Superbug plans have doubled, but few countries are delivering
summary: More countries are drawing up plans to tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), but major gaps in testing and treatment mean billions of people continue to be at risk, according to new data released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Monday.

title: Lebanon leading the way in mental health support
summary: Mental health support must be a core part of the humanitarian response, said the UN Deputy Secretary-General during a visit to Lebanon over the weekend, where efforts to address the psychological toll of years of conflict and instability offer valuable lessons for other crisis-affected countries.

title: AI gets climate science right – until users push back
summary: The best AI models answer most climate science questions correctly, but they often abandon established facts as soon as a user disagrees, according to a new report co-authored by the UN.

title: Syria: Progress ‘real’ but fragile, as remnants of war wreck young lives
summary: Syria is showing “undeniable signs of progress” nearly two years after the fall of the Assad regime, but explosive ordnance, the approaching winter and severe funding shortfalls threaten those fragile gains, senior UN officials told the Security Council on Monday.

title: COP31 enters decisive week as climate talks face political test and AI initiatives gather pace
summary: New international initiatives on artificial intelligence and green industrialization showcased technology’s growing role in climate action, even as negotiators remained deadlocked on finance, fossil fuels and adaptation ahead of the final stretch of the UN talks.

title: Funding cuts raise risks of trafficking and exploitation for refugee children
summary: Sharp reductions in humanitarian funding are putting refugees, particularly children, at increased risk of being trafficked, exploited or abused, while the systems that protect them are weakening.

title: Guterres calls for a legally binding instrument for ‘killer robots'
summary: Talks began in Geneva on Monday to push for controls on lethal autonomous weapons systems that are often referred to as “killer robots”.

title: At his final ASEAN Summit, Guterres upholds cooperation and action on Myanmar
summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres underscored the need for stronger collaboration with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and an end to the crisis in Myanmar, in remarks to regional leaders meeting in the Philippine capital Manila on Monday.

title: First Person: Managing risk on Ukraine’s frontline
summary: Humanitarian workers providing support to communities on the frontline of the war between Ukraine and Russia must balance remaining close to those in need with the heightened risks of operating in a warzone, according to the top UN official in Ukraine.

title: Empowering faith and Indigenous leaders to combat hate
summary: Religious, traditional and Indigenous leaders need to be empowered to act as full partners in preventing conflict, not just praised for their role, speakers said Sunday at the opening of the Muscat Plan of Action Forum in Oman.
